source_refs.title: Connect to Wi-Fi on your iPhone or iPad
source_refs.applicability: iPhone; the page covers iPhone and iPad, this ref uses only the iPhone steps. Password or terms acceptance may be required; the page says to ask the network administrator if the password is not known.
source_refs.verified_excerpt: Tap the name of the Wi-Fi network that you want to join.
source_refs.model_visible_text: On iPhone: Open Settings and select 'Wi-Fi', then switch Wi-Fi on. The phone automatically searches for nearby networks. Select the network you want. You may first need to enter its password or accept its terms and conditions. If you don't know the password, ask your network administrator. Check for a blue tick beside the network name and the Wi-Fi icon in the top corner of the screen. This confirms the connection. Optional: For a more reliable connection that uses cellular data alongside Wi-Fi, scroll down and turn on 'Connectivity Assist.'

source_refs.title: Connect to Wi-Fi networks on your Android device
source_refs.applicability: Android devices; the page gives these steps without a version limit. Networks with a lock icon require a password.
source_refs.model_visible_text: On Android: Open the Settings app. Tap 'Network & internet', then 'Internet'. Tap a listed network. Networks with a lock icon require a password. If the network is nearby but not listed, wait for the list to refresh. If the network still isn't listed, scroll to the bottom and tap 'Add network'. Enter the network name (SSID) and security details, then tap 'Save'. Hidden network: Tap 'Advanced options', set 'Hidden Network' to 'Yes', then tap 'Save'.
source_refs.extraction_method: WebFetch of the official page on 2026-11-17; steps paraphrased from the named sections (Turn on & connect; branches listed under the same page); straight apostrophes used; excerpt quoted as WebFetch returned it

source_refs.title: Connect to a Wi-Fi network in Windows
source_refs.section: Connect to a Wi-Fi network (Windows 11 steps)
source_refs.verified_excerpt: Choose the Wi-Fi network you want, then select Connect.
source_refs.model_visible_text: On Windows 11: Select the Network, Sound, or Battery icons on the taskbar to open Quick Settings. A Disconnected icon appears when you're not connected. In the Wi-Fi quick setting, select 'Manage Wi-Fi connections'. Choose the Wi-Fi network you want, then select 'Connect'. If the network you expect isn't listed, select the 'Refresh network list' button in the lower right to start a new scan. If prompted, type the network password, then select 'Next'.

source_refs.title: Connect your Mac to the internet using Wi-Fi
source_refs.applicability: Mac; the page lists these conditions: Wi-Fi turned on, within range of the network, password ready
source_refs.verified_excerpt: If you’re within range of a Wi-Fi network, you can try to join it.
source_refs.model_visible_text: On Mac: Wi-Fi must be turned on. You need to be within range of the network. Have the network's password ready. If you're within range of a Wi-Fi network, you can try to join it. Click the Wi-Fi status menu icon in the menu bar, then select the network. If you don't see it, choose 'Other Networks' to list nearby networks. If prompted, enter the password and click 'Join'.

source_refs.title: Connect your Chromebook to Wi-Fi
source_refs.section: Connect your Chromebook to Wi-Fi (steps for open and secure networks)
source_refs.applicability: Chromebook; this ref uses open and secure network steps only
source_refs.verified_excerpt: To connect to the internet, turn on your Chromebook's Wi-Fi and use a compatible network.
source_refs.model_visible_text: On Chromebook: Select the time in the bottom-right tray, then select the Settings gear. In the left menu, select Network, then Wi-Fi. Turn on Wi-Fi. Your Chromebook lists nearby networks. Select the network you want. For an open or public network, select 'Connect'. You may be prompted to open a sign-in page in your browser. For a secure network, enter the network password, then select 'Connect'.

source_refs.title: Connect your Samsung Galaxy to the Internet
source_refs.applicability: Samsung Galaxy phones; the page applies to devices sold in Canada and says screens and settings may vary by carrier, software version, and model
source_refs.verified_excerpt: Wi-Fi must be activated to see available networks.
source_refs.model_visible_text: On Samsung Galaxy: Open Settings and tap 'Connections'. Tap 'Wi-Fi'. Turn on the Wi-Fi toggle if it's off. Wi-Fi must be activated to see available networks. Tap the name of the network you want. If the network is password-protected, enter the password and tap 'Connect'. A password-protected network requires you to have its password first. When connected, the network name appears under 'Current network', with 'Connected' below it.
